|-------|----------------|
| **Aircraft in discussion** | Unmanned aircraft (everyday speech: “drones”), helicopters, and **eVTOL** concepts — **electric vertical take-off and landing** craft |
| **Physical infrastructure** | Take-off and landing sites (industry label: **vertiports**), charging, maintenance |
| **Digital infrastructure** | Communications, traffic-management software, data platforms |
| **Applications** | Logistics, inspection, emergency response, passenger transport, supporting finance and insurance |

### LAE, UAM, and AAM terms {#t01-lae-uam-aam}

| Term | Meaning in this course |
|------|-------------------------|
| **LAE (low-altitude economy)** | The umbrella: economic activity in low-altitude airspace plus the supporting ecosystem. |
| [**UAM (urban air mobility)**](glossary.qmd#uam) | A *subset*: moving people or cargo over short distances **inside** a dense city. |
| [**AAM (advanced air mobility)**](glossary.qmd#aam) | A broader industry label for new aircraft connecting cities to suburbs or other corridors. |

Teaching table from the week notes. [LAE, UAM, and AAM](week-01.qmd#3-lae-uam-and-aam)

### Mission-family economics {#t01-mission-family-economics}

| Family | Typical value created | Typical binding constraints (preview) |
|--------|----------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Cargo / logistics | Time, reliability, access where roads are slow or blocked | Payload, weather, landing sites, BVLOS / advanced-ops permission ([**BVLOS**](glossary.qmd#bvlos) = beyond visual line of sight) |
| Passenger mobility | Door-to-door time vs MTR / taxi / Airport Express | Vertiport access, load factor, noise, public acceptance |
| Inspection | Lower disruption and risk vs manned access | Safety case, data / privacy, repeatability |
| Emergency / public | Outcomes that alternatives cannot match in time | Priority rules, funding (availability vs usage), acceptance |

Teaching table from the week notes. [How to read each family economically](week-01.qmd#how-to-read-each-family-economically)

| NPV result (under stated assumptions) | Interpretation |
|---------------------------------------|----------------|
| Positive | Project may be financially attractive |
| Negative | Does not justify the investment |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Net present value (NPV)](week-01.qmd#net-present-value-npv)

### Door-to-door friction (smooth vs shock) {#t01-door-to-door-friction}

| | Case A: smooth journey | Case B: friction shock |
|--|------------------------|-------------------------|
| Flight time | 10 minutes | 10 minutes |
| Boarding and waiting | 5 minutes | 25 minutes |
| Total journey | 15 minutes | 35 minutes |
| Time saved vs a 45-minute alternative | 30 minutes = 0.5 h | 10 minutes ≈ 0.167 h |
| Value of time saved | $1000\times 0.5 =$ **HK$500** | $1000\times 0.167 \approx$ **HK$167** |

Teaching table from the week notes. [8.1 Door-to-door friction destroys value](week-01.qmd#8-1-door-to-door-friction-destroys-value)

### Roles in the LAE chain {#t01-roles}

| Role | Plain meaning |
|------|----------------|
| [**OEM**](glossary.qmd#oem) | **Original equipment manufacturer** — produces the aircraft or key components. |
| **Vertiport / sites** | Take-off, landing, passenger or cargo handling, charging, related ground operations (industry language; no dedicated Hong Kong vertiport statute yet). |
| **UTM / U-space** | Digital services and procedures that support safe, efficient management of unmanned operations. **UTM** = unmanned aircraft system traffic management. **U-space** is an EU / industry frame, **not** Hong Kong law; Hong Kong’s Smart Low-altitude Traffic Management System is a **planned** programme (Policy Address language: progressive implementation from **2028**), not a statute yet ([Key numbers](key-figures.qmd); [Glossary · airspace](glossary.qmd#airspace-and-traffic)). |
| **Operator** | Provides the transport, logistics, inspection, or public service to the customer. |
| **Customers / public agencies** | Pay for missions or sponsor public-service outcomes. |
| **Supporting services** | Finance, leasing, insurance, certification, legal and professional services. |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Roles](week-01.qmd#roles)

## Week 2 — Market structure and competition {#week-02}

Full notes: [Week 2](week-02.qmd) · 9 tables below.

### Market structures (plain meanings) {#t02-market-structures}

| Structure | Plain meaning | Everyday analogy (not an LAE claim) |
|-----------|---------------|-------------------------------------|
| **Monopoly** | One provider serves the defined market. Pricing power is still limited by demand, regulation, and substitutes. | A single toll tunnel on a route |
| **Oligopoly** | A small number of large players watch each other; one price cut can trigger responses. | A handful of mobile networks |
| **Perfect competition** | Many small sellers of a homogeneous product; no one can raise price alone. | Many stalls selling the same simple item |

Teaching table from the week notes. [What economists mean by “market structure”](week-02.qmd#2-what-economists-mean-by-market-structure)

### Competitive logic by segment {#t02-competitive-logic-segment}

| Segment | Likely rivalry style | Scarce asset often binding | Softens / intensifies price pressure |
|---------|----------------------|----------------------------|--------------------------------------|
| Last-mile logistics | Many routes; cost and reliability | Pads, BVLOS permission, weather windows | Homogeneous parcels → more Bertrand-like if capacity loose |
| Passenger air taxis | Few corridors; brand and schedule | Vertiport slots, noise windows | Differentiation + pad caps can soften wars |
| Inspection | Project / contract markets | Certified capability, data/privacy | Less pure price war; quality and safety cases matter |
| EMS / public | Often procurement / priority rules | Availability, response time | Willingness to pay high; access may be allocated, not auctioned |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Competitive logic by segment (textbook table)](week-02.qmd#competitive-logic-by-segment-textbook-table)

### HHI worked shares {#t02-hhi-worked}

| | Case A: four equal operators | Case B: one large, one small |
|--|------------------------------|------------------------------|
| Shares | 25%, 25%, 25%, 25% | 80%, 20% |
| HHI | $4 \times 25^2 = \mathbf{2{,}500}$ | $80^2 + 20^2 = 6{,}400 + 400 = \mathbf{6{,}800}$ |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Worked illustration (classroom shares)](week-02.qmd#worked-illustration-classroom-shares)

| + Marginal cost | HK$50 | HK$50 |
| [**ATC**](glossary.qmd#atc-average-total-cost) (average total cost) | **HK$1,717** | **HK$217** |

### Capacity vs price war {#t02-capacity-vs-price-war}

| | Unconstrained fleets | Each limited to 30 flights/day (total 60 < 100) |
|--|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| Logic | Undercutting can push $P$ toward **HK$100** | Neither can absorb all demand; price pressure **may** be weaker |
| Lesson | Price war destroys margins | Scarcity can support margins — not a promise of $P =$ HK$500 |

## Week 3 — Cost, revenue, and breakeven {#week-03}

Full notes: [Week 3](week-03.qmd) · 10 tables below.

### CAPEX vs OPEX {#t03-capex-vs-opex}

| Label | Plain meaning | Typical LAE examples |
|-------|---------------|----------------------|
| [**CAPEX**](glossary.qmd#capex-opex) (capital expenditure) | Investment in assets that provide benefits over several years | Aircraft, charging equipment, vertiport construction, major software platforms |
| [**OPEX**](glossary.qmd#capex-opex) (operating expenditure) | Recurring spend to operate the service | Energy, maintenance, staff, insurance, site fees, communications, routine compliance |

Teaching table from the week notes. [CAPEX vs OPEX](week-03.qmd#capex-vs-opex)

### Investment level and unit cost {#t03-investment-unit-cost}

| | Case A: HK$10M investment | Case B: HK$6M investment |
|--|----------------------------|---------------------------|
| Daily asset allocation | $10\text{M}/1{,}825 \approx$ **HK$5,479** | $6\text{M}/1{,}825 \approx$ **HK$3,288** |
| + Daily OPEX | HK$8,000 | HK$8,000 |
| Total daily economic cost | HK$13,479 | HK$11,288 |
| **Cost per mission** | $\approx$ **HK$270** | $\approx$ **HK$226** |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Worked illustration (investment level and unit cost)](week-03.qmd#worked-illustration-investment-level-and-unit-cost)

### Cost stack to unit economics (tool chain) {#t03-cost-stack-toolchain}

| Question | Tool this week | Week 2 cousin |
|----------|----------------|---------------|
| What did we buy? | CAPEX / residual / useful days | Sunk site cost |
| What burns if we fly zero? | Fixed OPEX | Fixed cost in ATC |
| What rises with each mission? | Variable cost | Marginal cost |
| Cost of capacity offered? | CASK | ATC at a given utilization |
| How many units to survive? | Breakeven / required missions | Density needed to lower ATC |

Teaching table from the week notes. [From cost stack to unit economics (tool chain)](week-03.qmd#3-from-cost-stack-to-unit-economics-tool-chain)

## Week 5 — Sites, slots, and networks {#week-05}

Full notes: [Week 5](week-05.qmd) · 10 tables below.

### Three classroom vertiport archetypes {#t05-vertiport-archetypes}

| Archetype | Plain idea | Typical trade-off |
|-----------|------------|-------------------|
| **Building-based** | Rooftop or elevated structure | Strong access; structural, safety, power, and circulation upgrades |
| **Integrated hub** | Multiple pads/stands plus charging, processing, maintenance | High capability; high cost and complexity |
| **Ground-based** | Available land site | Often easier to expand; may mean longer access to customers |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Three classroom vertiport archetypes](week-05.qmd#2-three-classroom-vertiport-archetypes)

| Daily infrastructure allocation | HK$5,000 | HK$1,000 |
| Daily OPEX | HK$8,000 | HK$2,000 |
| Extra access time | 8 min | 3 min |
| Access burden | $8 \times 15 \times 100 =$ HK$12,000 | $3 \times 15 \times 100 =$ HK$4,500 |
| **Generalized site cost/day** | **HK$25,000** | **HK$7,500** |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Worked illustration (two archetypes)](week-05.qmd#worked-illustration-two-archetypes)

### Higher- vs lower-cost site {#t05-higher-lower-cost-site}

## Week 6 — Partnerships and payment design {#week-06}

Full notes: [Week 6](week-06.qmd) · 7 tables below.

### Three business-model archetypes {#t06-business-model-archetypes}

| Archetype | Core idea | Typical exposure |
|-----------|-----------|------------------|
| **Asset-intensive operator** | Owns or finances major aircraft and infrastructure; controls more of the operating system | High capital and utilization risk; potentially greater control and value capture |
| **Service integrator** | Promises an outcome (e.g. delivery availability, inspection coverage) while leasing assets or contracting operators | Lower asset ownership; high coordination and performance risk |
| **Platform orchestrator** | Connects customers, operators, infrastructure, and data services | Fewer physical assets; software, cybersecurity, compliance, customer acquisition, and network risk |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Three business-model archetypes](week-06.qmd#2-three-business-model-archetypes)

| Partner / operator payouts | HK$0 | HK$800k | HK$700k |
| **Economic profit** | **HK$467k** | **HK$100k** | **HK$117k** |
| Character | High capital & utilization exposure | Supplier dependency | Network & governance risk |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Worked illustration (three archetypes)](week-06.qmd#worked-illustration-three-archetypes)

| **Operating result** | **Loss HK$260k** | **Profit HK$150k** (before deductions) |

| **European U-space** | Regulatory and digital-service frame for unmanned operations in designated airspace |
| **United States** | FAA / interagency coordination of certification, operations, airspace, infrastructure, environment, community engagement |

### Term-sheet issues (authority vs operator) {#t06-term-sheet-issues}

| Issue | Public authority typically wants | Operator typically wants |
|-------|----------------------------------|--------------------------|
| Service outcome | Reliable, affordable delivery of the mission | Clear, measurable scope |
| Payment | Value for money; budget control | Bankable, predictable cash flow |
| Performance | Strong KPIs and remedies | Controllable targets; fair relief |
| Risk | Transfer where value improves | Accept only manageable, priced risk |
| Flexibility | Ability to adapt the public service | Compensation for material changes |

| **European Union** | Harmonized UAS rules; U-space framework for designated airspace and certified service providers |

### Regulatory-pathway scorecard {#t07-pathway-scorecard}

| Dimension | Managerial question |
|-----------|---------------------|
| Clarity | Are requirements and decision points understandable? |
| Proportionality | Are controls matched to operational risk? |
| Evidence pathway | Can testing generate useful evidence? |
| Predictability | Are process, timing, and responsibilities credible? |
| Scalability | Can the approval support expansion or repetition? |
| Interoperability | Can evidence or approvals support other markets? |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Regulatory-pathway scorecard](week-07.qmd#regulatory-pathway-scorecard)

### Phased regulatory roadmap {#t07-phased-reg-roadmap}

| Phase | Operating scope | Evidence collected | Expansion gate |
|-------|-----------------|--------------------|----------------|
| 1. Controlled test | Limited route, time, and payload | Communications, navigation, weather, procedures | Safety and reliability thresholds met |
| 2. Extended trial | More operating conditions or users | Repeated performance and stakeholder feedback | Approved review and updated controls |
| 3. Scaled operation | Wider route, frequency, or fleet | Ongoing monitoring and incident reporting | Continued compliance and periodic review |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Phased regulatory roadmap](week-07.qmd#9-phased-regulatory-roadmap)

| **Obtainable demand** | Portion the operator may realistically serve after competition and capacity constraints |

### Funnel → contribution (steps) {#t09-funnel-contribution-steps}

| Step | Figure |
|------|--------|
| Relevant trips | 20,000/day |
| Eligible time-sensitive segment | 10% → $SAM = 2{,}000$ |
| Expected choice share | 15% → $D_{\mathrm{pot}} =$ **300** passenger-trips/day |
| Reliable capacity | 80 flights/day × 4 seats × 80% load = **256** |
| **Served demand** | $\min\{300,256\}=$ **256** passenger-trips/day |

| **Contribution** | **HK\$71,680** | **≈ HK\$23.7M** |

| Governance | Complaints resolved on time | Defined process and deadline |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Sustainability KPI design](week-10.qmd#8-sustainability-kpi-design)

## Week 11 — Synthesis and recommendation {#week-11}

Full notes: [Week 11](week-11.qmd) · 6 tables below.

### Capacity shock (viability) {#t11-capacity-shock}

| | Base case | Capacity shock ($K = 80$) |
|--|-----------|--------------------------------------|
| Served activity | $\min\{100,100\}=100$ | $\min\{100,80\}=80$ |
| Operating profit | $(600-100)\times 100 - 40{,}000$ = **HK\$10,000/day** | $(600-100)\times 80 - 40{,}000$ = **HK\$0/day** |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Worked illustration (capacity shock)](week-11.qmd#worked-illustration-capacity-shock)

### Airport-corridor screening chain {#t11-airport-corridor-screening}

| Block | Example reasoning |
|-------|-------------------|
| Problem | Test whether a time-sensitive airport segment values the proposed door-to-door service |
| Demand | Estimate customer choice at alternative fares using generalized cost and capacity constraints |
| Operations | Define aircraft, seats, load factor, operating days, turnaround, and serviceable capacity |
| Economics | Contribution per passenger-trip, fixed cost, breakeven, NPV, downside cash need |
| Regulation | Identify applicable permissions; use evidence-based **Sandbox X** or **AC-013** milestones **only where relevant** (keep programmes distinct) |
| Impact | Life-cycle emissions, noise exposure, privacy controls, access, public-service effects |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Airport-corridor screening (illustrative chain)](week-11.qmd#airport-corridor-screening-illustrative-chain)

### Risk register and decision triggers {#t11-risk-register}

| Risk | Model channel | Response | Decision trigger |
|------|---------------|----------|------------------|
| Demand | Choice share and price | Pilot and staged capacity | Minimum verified demand |
| Weather | Serviceable capacity | Procedures and resilience | Reliability threshold |
| Regulation | Scope and timing | Evidence plan and review | Permission or milestone |
| Technology | Cost and availability | Test, redundancy, supplier plan | Performance threshold |
| Community impact | Route and operating conditions | Mitigation and engagement | Exposure and complaint KPI |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Risk register and decision-gated roadmap](week-11.qmd#4-risk-register-and-decision-gated-roadmap)

### Decision-maker lenses {#t11-decision-maker-lenses}

| Lens | Core question |
|------|---------------|
| **Operational credibility** | Can the service be delivered safely and reliably? |
| **Commercial viability** | Are demand, contribution, cash flow, and financing assumptions credible? |
| **Regulatory feasibility** | Is the proposed pathway specific to the aircraft and operation? |
| **Public value** | Are benefits, costs, access, and distribution addressed? |
| **Decision quality** | Does the recommendation acknowledge uncertainty, alternatives, and conditions for revision? |

Teaching table from the week notes. [The decision-maker's lens](week-11.qmd#5-the-decision-maker-s-lens)

### 12-minute decision pitch {#t11-twelve-minute-pitch}

| Segment | Focus |
|---------|--------|
| **Decision and value proposition (≈2 min)** | Problem, recommendation, customer, use case, principal evidence |
| **Integrated quantitative case (≈4 min)** | Demand, reliable capacity, contribution, breakeven, NPV, one clear sensitivity |
| **Implementation and governance (≈3 min)** | Infrastructure, partners, regulatory pathway, responsibilities, decision gates |
| **Risk and impact (≈2 min)** | Major downside, mitigation, residual risk, sustainability, distribution |
| **Closing decision (≈1 min)** | Requested action, next milestone, funding or approval need, stop conditions |

Teaching table from the week notes. [A 12-minute decision pitch](week-11.qmd#a-12-minute-decision-pitch)

### Weak vs strong evidence {#t11-weak-vs-strong}

| Weak case | Strong case |
|-----------|-------------|
| Uses total market size as forecast demand | Defines the market and competing alternative |
| Confuses passenger-trips, flights, and seats | Checks demand against reliable capacity |
| Applies repeated percentage haircuts | Maps each constraint to one model channel |
| Reports expected profit without downside risk | Reports NPV, probability of loss, and cash need |
| Assumes approval, acceptance, and insurance outcomes | States evidence, limitations, and decision gates |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Weak vs strong evidence](week-11.qmd#weak-vs-strong-evidence)

| **Candidate links** | **6** | **≈29** |

| | No demonstrated improvement | Improved risk case |
|--|----------------------------|--------------------|
| Premium | HK\$12.5M | HK\$9M (illustrative) |
| Evidence / control cost | HK\$0 | HK\$3M |
| **Total** | **HK\$12.5M** | **HK\$12M** (first-year saving HK\$0.5M) |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Value of better risk evidence (illustrative)](week-12.qmd#value-of-better-risk-evidence-illustrative)

### Leasing appraisal (operator vs lessor) {#t12-leasing-appraisal}

| | Operator | Lessor |
|--|----------|--------|
| Situation | Revenue after disruption HK\$250k; lease HK\$300k | Contractual receipt HK\$300k; financing/asset-management HK\$150k |
| Result | Shortfall HK\$50k before other costs; bears demand/operating risk | Cash flow HK\$150k before credit loss; **default puts receipt and asset value at risk** |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Leasing appraisal (risk does not disappear)](week-12.qmd#leasing-appraisal-risk-does-not-disappear)

### Quantitative toolkit recap {#t12-toolkit-recap}

| Question type | Typical tools |
|---------------|---------------|
| Demand | Generalized cost, choice share, elasticity, market funnel |
| Capacity | Reliable flights, seats/payload, operating days, bottlenecks |
| Economics | Contribution, breakeven, unit cost, cash flow, NPV |
| Uncertainty | Scenarios, sensitivity, expected value, probability of loss, liquidity need |
| Allocation | Queues, reservations, priority, congestion charges, auctions |
| Impact | Life-cycle emissions, noise exposure, privacy controls, distribution, KPIs |

Teaching table from the week notes. [Quantitative toolkit recap](week-12.qmd#quantitative-toolkit-recap)
